body:
Raised and independently reproduced 2026-10-07 America/Los_Angeles by post-merge Auditor `01a10892-0782-7b13-902c-d8b4db6c155d`.

Affected PR #1131, merge `bb3ac9f8855b400fc3e3de46029080e24aed4e52`, head `8baa34fa7030b88e411a11e842ae257298e1be31`. Preserve closed #1122/#444 and original #940 evidence, dates and source limits. One additive geography erratum PR in the disjoint namespace below; do not rewrite the original validator or historical receipts.

Evidence and defects:
1. `validate_pointer_evidence` builds `entries = {row.get('id'): row for row in records.get('objects', [])}` and checks only the set of dictionary keys. It silently collapses duplicate source records while its error message promises duplicate rejection. In the actual unchanged `__main__`, append an exact copy of the final `chl-adm3-metaData-txt` record to the complete six-record ledger: seven records/six identities are accepted, all ten built-in controls pass, and the result reports six verified records. Pointer OID/size/path evidence is correct for the original six records; this is an integrity gap, not proof that original source bytes are wrong. A separate preserved attempt duplicating the first record fails later because its last-wins duplicate masks the built-in wrong-vintage mutation; it does not establish a reliable duplicate preflight.
2. The final output loop calls `Path.write_bytes` for six existing owned historical products, followed by `reproducibility.json`. It has no complete fresh destination admission. The actual entry point overwrites all seven owned private sentinel files in the isolated reproduction described below. Default execution would replace original retained evidence; no overwrite of originals was performed by the Auditor.
3. `reproducibility.json` is generated by assigning both `run_one_sha256` and `run_two_sha256` to the aggregate of the same single invocation, with `outcome: passed`. One actual fresh invocation already emits that purported comparison. It neither consumes nor compares a second run. The Auditor separately performed two full fresh runs and found all seven products byte-identical to each other and retained originals; that genuine result does not repair the program's unsupported standalone comparison claim.

Actual reproduction: managed sparse detached exact-merge slot; Python 3.12.14/Shapely 2.1.2/GEOS 3.13.1; bytecode disabled, no dependency installation or raw-source hydration. Reviewed adapter redirects only seven exact final Path.write_bytes destinations and their generated-output reads into owned private output directories. The duplicate case additionally intercepts only the exact pointer-ledger text read with a retained complete byte fixture. Original code, imports, Git baseline reads, old checker subprocess and calculations are unchanged. Two full fresh mains produce all seven products exactly matching retained bytes. A full duplicate-last-record main succeeds. Existing-output main uses seven private sentinels and the actual final writer semantics, preserving every original. Failed attempts and complete fixtures/outputs remain preserved. No production/import/boundary action.

Success criteria:
- Add a bounded erratum entry point and evidence in the new owned namespace; preserve all historical source packets, code, outputs, dates, identities and original issue history.
- Validate the complete six-record source roster before collapsing/joining records. Reject duplicate/foreign/missing records, inconsistent pointer path/vintage/hash/size fields, and duplicate records in different positions with meaningful actual-entry-point controls. Bind the complete actually consumed source-ledger bytes and code/input receipts to the result.
- Admit the entire fresh owned seven-product destination set before any write; reject existing files/directories/broken symlinks and path escapes while preserving originals and existing contents. Exercise actual entry points and partial/conflicting destination cases.
- Produce two independently executed complete runs; compare their full product sets before issuing a passed reproducibility receipt. A single run, missing/failed second run or mismatched products must not claim a matched pair. Bind actual code/input/output bytes and execution identities, preserving original-vintage receipts.
- Retain and reproduce the exact230 subjects, 53ARGADM2/177CHLADM3, 29parents, 242baseline components, two documented historical component-field omissions, retained116/113/1 dispositions and228 matched rows. Reproduce old false-parent acceptance/new rejection and the nine existing meaningful negative cases. No source-derived IoU/geographic/source-license certification.

Inspection supporting scope: all25added whole files377034B, all38 manifest baseline/source/output descriptors and11 metric bindings reconcile. Independent actual pinned GeoJSON/hierarchy checks verify every230 baseline identity/name/parent/source/type/validity/component field, corresponding assessment fields and retained cross-ledger values, summary rosters/dispositions and29parent counts. Six fresh authenticated upstream GitHub Contents API responses at `9469f09592ced973a3448cf66b6100b741b64c0d` decode to exactly the retained Git LFS pointers. Original asserted ARG/CHL raw hashes disagree with these authenticated pointer OIDs as reported. Raw LFS geometry, IGN/Subdere captures/reuse terms, Law1186, name variants and source-derived IoUs remain explicitly unverified under original #1122 acceptance; they are not dependencies for this bounded mechanical repair. No geography or production approval.

Deduplication: complete all-state issue pagination (14 pages, final48 entries,936 non-PR issues) and affected-packet later Git history find no existing duplicate/preservation/reproducibility repair for this validator. Closed1122 fixes old940 provenance/record binding; open937/938 own Argentina/Chile semantic candidates and do not own this new integrity correction. Existing1332 owns the different batch4 packet. Empty dependencies: required original code/baseline/source pointer bytes are available, and owned namespace is new and disjoint. Preserve other workers' claims and files.

Complete duplicate-last pointer fixture: SHA-256 `e7c9001573ce8657a3fac4c1e52d993f9aca48d66af5a5e3ca1b1dde10278c01`, 7992 bytes.
